From name:  Troy Wallace | Pristine Image Wellness
To:  Existing Pristine Image Med Spa client list (~8,000)
Subject (recommended):  A new metabolic option for our spa family
Subject (A/B alternate):  Why “trying harder” may not be the real problem
Preheader:  Introducing Feel Great + a free assessment to start — no hype.
Primary CTA (all buttons):  https://www.pristineimagewellness.com/free-assessment
Hi {First Name},
As a client of Pristine Image Med Spa, you already know how much we care that you don’t just look your best — you feel your best, too.
Today I’m excited to finally share something we’ve been working on behind the scenes. We waited until everything was in place before bringing it to our spa clients. Now we’re ready.

Through Pristine Image Wellness, we’re introducing the Feel Great protocol — a simple daily approach designed to support metabolic health and help you understand what may be happening beneath stubborn weight, cravings, low energy, and appetite struggles.
Curious what your metabolism may be telling you?
START MY FREE METABOLIC HEALTH ASSESSMENT →
If you’ve ever thought, “I’m eating better, trying harder, doing what I’m supposed to do… so why am I still struggling?” — you’re exactly who we had in mind.
For many people, the conversation needs to go deeper than calories and willpower. It needs to include metabolic health.
And there’s some fascinating new science behind it.

You’ve probably heard a lot about GLP-1 lately, because of medications such as Ozempic®, Wegovy®, and Mounjaro®. Here’s what often gets left out: your body already produces GLP-1 naturally. It’s a hormone made in your gut that plays a role in appetite, fullness, and metabolic signaling after you eat.
Prescription GLP-1 medications and food-based support are different tools. Those medications have their place for some people under a doctor’s care — and they are not what we’re offering.
What we are introducing is the Feel Great protocol: two products used together as part of a simple daily routine —
Unimate® — made with yerba maté
Balance — a specialized fiber blend
Together, they’re designed to support the normal gut and metabolic processes your body already runs.

In recent laboratory research using human gut microbes and GLP-1-producing cells, Unicity reports that the Feel Great combination more than doubled the GLP-1 response — about a 107% increase in that laboratory model.

That does not mean Feel Great is a prescription GLP-1 medication, and a laboratory result does not guarantee a specific outcome for any individual. But it’s exciting early research into how nutrition, the gut, and the body’s own metabolic signaling may work together.
Want to see whether this approach could make sense for you?
TAKE MY FREE METABOLIC HEALTH ASSESSMENT →
The assessment helps you look at patterns worth paying attention to, such as:
Stubborn weight that doesn’t respond the way it used to
Frequent cravings or constant thoughts about food
Energy crashes, especially during the day or after meals
Feeling hungry again shortly after eating
Difficulty feeling satisfied
Feeling like your body is working against your efforts
The goal is to help you understand what may be going on first. From there, we can talk about your next best step — and whether the Feel Great protocol is appropriate for you.
It only takes a few minutes to get started.
START MY FREE METABOLIC HEALTH ASSESSMENT →

We’re genuinely excited to introduce this to our Pristine Image Med Spa clients. You’ve trusted us with your care at the spa, and through Pristine Image Wellness we now have a way to help you explore another important part of feeling your best: your metabolic health.
If weight, cravings, appetite, or energy have been frustrating you — even when you feel like you’re doing everything right — I encourage you to start with the assessment.
YES — I WANT TO UNDERSTAND MY METABOLIC HEALTH →
With care,
Troy Wallace
Pristine Image Med Spa · Pristine Image Wellness

P.S. You don’t need to wait until something feels “bad enough” to start understanding your metabolic health. If you’ve been wondering why your body doesn’t respond the way it used to, take a few minutes and complete the free assessment today. Start here: https://www.pristineimagewellness.com/free-assessment

TikTok Competitor & Content Benchmark Review
Capture date: August 4, 2026   |   Platform in scope: TikTok only   |   Founder: Troy Wallace, Tyler, TX
Executive Summary
Three accounts were reviewed as content benchmarks. They were selected for their content systems and niche relevance, not because all three compete for the same Tyler, Texas clients.
The reviewed content from all three accounts was predominantly face-led educational video rather than static graphics, and all three taught in plain language with strong on-screen clarity.
The repeatable system — one clear idea per video, a recurring series, and a single consistent call to action — is what PIW should copy.
What PIW should not copy: fear-first organ messaging, cure claims, unapproved product claims, and insulin-resistance-led positioning.
This review covered TikTok only. It cannot show how these accounts perform on other platforms, and no conversion data was available.
Scope and Method
This is a TikTok-only competitor review carried out in a single live session on August 4, 2026. Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Pinterest and YouTube were out of scope. Research was observation-only.

All metrics are point-in-time and change daily. Follower counts were verified via live user search. Post metrics come from live search and browse surfaces. Where a figure was not visible it is written as not publicly visible.
Some direct profile deep-links intermittently returned a wait or error state under rate limits during the session.

Market context note: These accounts lean heavily on insulin and glucose education. That is documented here as competitive market reality. PIW content strategy still prefers non-IR-led entry points — plateau, fatigue, myths and progress beyond the scale — until Troy directs otherwise.
Selected Competitor and Content Benchmarks
These accounts were selected for their content systems and niche relevance. They do not all directly compete for the same Tyler, Texas clients.
1. Metabolic Boss (Dana Estelle)
Classification: Closest strategic competitor / niche benchmark
Profile: @metabolicboss
Audience size: 343.3K followers · 2.4M likes (live user search, 2026-08-04)

Recurring patterns: Face-led root-cause education; condition bridges (kidney, blood pressure, fatty liver, diabetes tags); keyword-comment calls to action; heavy hashtag SEO; urgency paired with hope. Frequency: multi-post library.
PIW takeaway: The call-to-action system and face-led education are transferable. Avoid the organ-fear framing and cure claims.
2. Justin / Stop Spiking Sugar
Classification: Top niche content benchmark
Profile: @insulinresistant1
Audience size: 1.9M followers · 17.7M likes (live user search, 2026-08-04)

Recurring patterns: Continuous glucose monitor and food-experiment series ("X and my blood sugar"); recipes that "won't spike"; food-order tests; product and affiliate mentions on some posts; high-volume experiment library.
PIW takeaway: Proof and experiment storytelling is powerful. Stay compliance-safe and make no unapproved product claims.
3. Glucose Goddess (Jessie Inchauspé)
Classification: Admired authority page / large-scale content benchmark
Profile: @glucosegoddess_
Audience size: 632.8K followers · 3M likes (live user search, 2026-08-04)

Recurring patterns: Polished science storytelling; one idea per video; myth and mechanism corrections; collaboration clips; high brand consistency; less hard keyword CTA and more authority plus book and brand funnel.
PIW takeaway: Plain-language mechanism education with high production clarity.

Also observed, outside the three benchmarks: a Philippine clinician education cluster (Doc Alvin, Dr Kilimanguru) producing strong local-language metabolism content under a different geography and offer model.
Post Analysis
Six posts were reviewed across the three accounts. Screenshots for each are held in the evidence appendix at the end of this report so they do not interrupt the analysis.
Post 1 — Metabolic Boss (@metabolicboss)
Link: https://www.tiktok.com/@metabolicboss/video/7582752998460329224
Visible metrics: Likes 7,874 | Comments 284 | Bookmarks 2,690 | Shares not publicly visible
Source of metrics: Visible on the live post page during browse, 2026-08-04

Why this post worked: Keyword-comment call to action appears designed to move viewers from educational content into a DM conversation. A condition-bridge entry hooks a feared problem and then points to a single root-cause narrative, backed by face-led authority.
Trends used: Keyword-comment CTA; root-cause bridge; condition-specific entry (#ckd); original sound voiceover; face-to-camera education.
PIW takeaway: Learn the CTA system, not the fear-first organ claims. READY maps cleanly to assessment invites without cure language.
Post 2 — Metabolic Boss (@metabolicboss)
Link: https://www.tiktok.com/@metabolicboss/video/7580134306190839058
Visible metrics: Search-card views 6,532. Likes and comments not publicly visible during live open.
Source of metrics: TikTok search video results card, 2026-08-04

Why this post worked: Stacks several high-anxiety health tags into one short education post, maximising multi-search discovery. A minimal caption relies on hashtag SEO. The pattern is one mechanism opening many doors.
Trends used: Hashtag stacking; multi-condition discovery; short educational clip; insulin-resistance narrative (documented as market context, not a PIW lead pillar).
PIW takeaway: Hashtag discipline is worth copying. The insulin-resistance framing is not recommended as a PIW lead pillar.
Post 3 — Justin / Stop Spiking Sugar (@insulinresistant1)
Link: https://www.tiktok.com/@insulinresistant1/video/7558942292866829586
Visible metrics: Comments 248 | Search-card views 22.9K. Likes not publicly visible as a separate counter.
Source of metrics: Comments visible during live browse; view count from TikTok search card, 2026-08-04

Why this post worked: A practical recipe combined with a glucose promise produces save-and-share content. Personal experiment branding builds trust without a clinic setting, and the series library encourages viewers to binge similar tests.
Trends used: Recipe-as-proof; blood sugar and glucose series; CGM-adjacent education; personal experiment format.
PIW takeaway: Series structure and everyday practicality transfer well. Skip the glucose-outcome promise.
Post 4 — Justin / Stop Spiking Sugar (@insulinresistant1)
Link: https://www.tiktok.com/@insulinresistant1/video/7164164024437837061
Visible metrics: Search-card views 194.8K, labelled Top liked. Likes and comments not publicly visible.
Source of metrics: TikTok search card on account video search, 2026-08-04

Why this post worked: The highest observed search-card view in his recent listing set during this session. The food-order idea is immediately usable and highly shareable, and series numbering encourages watch-next behaviour.
Trends used: Food-order series; proof experiment; Top-liked evergreen; multi-tag niche SEO.
PIW takeaway: Evergreen, immediately usable ideas earn repeat search traffic. Keep claims educational.
Post 5 — Glucose Goddess (@glucosegoddess_)
Link: https://www.tiktok.com/@glucosegoddess_/video/7623496212469009677
Visible metrics: Likes 7,403 | Comments 39 | Bookmarks 3,039 | Shares not publicly visible
Source of metrics: Visible on the live post page during browse, 2026-08-04

Why this post worked: A single simple habit hook combined with science-brand authority. The high bookmark-to-comment ratio suggests strong save-for-later utility, and the conversation framing adds social proof.
Trends used: One-trick education; podcast and collaboration clip style; original educational sound.
PIW takeaway: One idea per video, plus collaboration formats, are directly transferable.
Post 6 — Glucose Goddess (@glucosegoddess_)
Link: https://www.tiktok.com/@glucosegoddess_/video/7662040024573168910
Visible metrics: Search-card views 45.8K, labelled Top liked. Likes and comments not publicly visible.
Source of metrics: TikTok search card on account video search, 2026-08-04
Why this post worked: Corrects a common nutrition belief with a precise mechanism in plain language. Curiosity plus correction drives comments and shares among health-interested audiences.
Trends used: Myth and mechanism explainer; nutrition science short; plain-language biochemistry.
PIW takeaway: Myth-and-mechanism correction is the single most transferable format in this report.

TikTok Trend Research
Trend Analysis #1
Date of analysis: August 4, 2026   |   Platform in scope: TikTok   |   Repeat every 30 days
Executive Summary
Face-led educational video — a clinician or founder speaking directly to camera — was the most consistently observed format across the research session.
Plateau, fatigue, mistakes and myth-versus-fact language were the densest audience entry points, and all four can be used without leading on insulin resistance.
Original voiceover and educational audio dominated the wellness examples reviewed. Viral music and dance audio were not prominent among the higher-performing examples in this session.
"Progress beyond the scale" is the strongest brand-fit theme observed and pairs naturally with the Free Metabolic Health Assessment.
This report records patterns observed during one live session. It does not measure trend growth rates, and no engagement figures were estimated.
A. Research Scope and Method

This report is based on a single live TikTok research session carried out on August 4, 2026. Fourteen search queries were run, more than 70 unique video URLs were collected, six or more hashtag pages were opened, and three or more original-sound links were captured. Explore was confirmed live for the Fitness & Health and Education categories.
TikTok was authenticated as @mtynn.0. The account was not confirmed as the Pristine Image Wellness business account.
Research was observation-only. No posts, likes, comments, follows or profile edits were made during the session.
Stated limitations
Some video deep-links did not fully load during the session. Where that happened, the metric shown is the TikTok search-card view count only.
Hashtag pages frequently displayed the title without the full post grid until further scrolling.
TikTok Creative Center trend tools required an additional login that was not available. Public search and Explore were used as the primary evidence surfaces.
No statistics were estimated or invented. Missing figures are marked as not publicly visible or not confirmed during the live research session.

Geographic validation note: The authenticated account surfaced a noticeable Filipino creator cluster. Those examples support format-level observations, but they do not by themselves prove local demand in Tyler, Texas. Validate the leading hooks and search terms from the PIW business account or a US-context session before finalizing the first 30-day content calendar.
Compliance note for PIW: No insulin-resistance-led content recommendations. No medical guarantees, cure claims, extreme promises, body shaming, or unverified transformations.
B. Frequently Observed Hashtags

C. Audio and Music Patterns Observed During Research

Wellness and education posts observed in this session commonly used original sounds and voiceover rather than chart music. Always verify commercial sound rights in TikTok Business before any paid amplification.
A. Original sound / talking-head voiceover
Dominant pattern across health education posts observed. Observed repeatedly during this research session.

Loaded example: @wellness_labb "What happens when you eat too fast?" — 2,721 likes, 33 comments, 733 bookmarks, 1,085 shares during live open. Sound: https://www.tiktok.com/music/original-sound-7665108283178683158
Additional FYP example: https://www.tiktok.com/music/original-sound-NoThingz-7455639432935295760

PIW adaptation: Troy talking-head or clinic B-roll with calm voiceover explaining why generic plans stall, closing on READY. Owning original audio also keeps a series visually and sonically consistent.
B. Soft motivational / brand library audio
Observed on a @gymshark discipline post surfaced by the plateau search. Single example observed; treat as a supporting style only.
PIW adaptation: subtle underscore only where it does not distract. Original voiceover is preferred for credibility.
C. Template-driven editing
An on-page CapCut affiliate panel appeared beside a loaded wellness video, indicating template-driven editing remains mainstream. Single example observed.
PIW adaptation: simple text-pop templates for myth-versus-fact lists, keeping the clean brand look.

Audio guidance: The evidence in this session supports original voiceover and educational audio as the better fit for PIW. Viral dance or chart audio was not prominent among the stronger wellness examples reviewed and remains a weak brand fit for metabolic education.

1. Executive Summary

Metabolic Boss (Dana Estelle) operates a high-scale educational brand built on one repeatable thesis: most chronic metabolic symptoms are downstream of insulin resistance and cellular dysfunction. That thesis is taught through short-form video, condition-bridge storytelling, and a disciplined comment-keyword → DM conversion loop. Public signals reviewed for this report: approximately 343.5K TikTok followers, 2.4M TikTok likes, and roughly 352K Facebook followers.

Pristine Image Wellness (PIW) already competes in the same problem category—insulin resistance, metabolic health, and lasting weight loss—with a clear conversion asset (free insulin resistance assessment) and an education/accountability model. Public Facebook presence at the time of review was early-stage (~39 followers). The strategic opportunity is not to clone Metabolic Boss’s product/discount funnel. It is to adopt their content operating system: one root narrative, multi-condition reach, educational frameworks, high-retention hooks, and conversation-led CTAs that feed PIW’s assessment and care path.
Primary recommendation

Run PIW social as a root-cause education engine (insulin resistance / metabolic repair) using condition-bridge Reels, face-led teaching, and keyword/comment or DM CTAs into the free assessment—not as scattered wellness tips or cold product ads.
2. Brand Positioning
Metabolic Boss
Positioning: Neuroscience-informed guide who helps people reverse insulin resistance and chronic disease naturally.
Authority stack: Neuroscience graduate credential + personal healing story + community results language + “clinically validated / nutraceutical” framing.
Category: Health & wellness education with a commercial backend (tools, discount links, DM fulfillment).
Core promise: Fix the root (insulin / cellular environment) so downstream conditions can improve.
Differentiation: Every condition (kidney, neuropathy, fatty liver, blood pressure, anemia, cognitive risk) routes back to one root cause.
Platform roles: TikTok for reach; Instagram & Facebook called out as main platforms in bio; site CTA HealYourCellsNow.com.
Facebook intro (observed): “Dana Estelle … reverse insulin resistance NATURALLY … Cellular healing, hormones, inflammation, detox … Msg me for help.”
Pristine Image Wellness (current)
Positioning (public FB): Helping people overcome insulin resistance, improve metabolic health, and achieve lasting weight loss through education, guidance, and accountability.
Primary offer: Free Insulin Resistance Assessment — pristineimagewellness.com/free-assessment.
Contact signals: 535 West Southwest Loop 323 · +1 940-594-6710 · troy@pristineimagewellness.com.
Also surfaces community (Skool) and story/funnel links alongside the main site.
Gap vs Metabolic Boss: Same problem space; much lower content velocity; fewer condition-bridge angles; less systematized hook/CTA library; early social proof footprint.

Positioning adaptation for PIW

Own this lane: “Metabolic root-cause care for people tired of symptom-chasing—education, assessment, and accountability that make insulin resistance understandable and actionable.” Borrow Metabolic Boss’s clarity and narrative discipline. Do not borrow unsubstantiated cure claims or a pure supplement-spam perception.
3. Messaging Style
Voice: Confident teacher; challenges symptom-only thinking; reassures that the body can improve when the metabolic environment improves.
Tone: Urgent but hopeful. Pattern: “Most people think X starts in the organ—it doesn’t.”
Clarity: Clinical terms (insulin resistance, inflammation, oxidative stress) explained in plain English immediately.
POV: First-person for story authority (“I dealt with burning pain…”) then second-person invitation (“If you’re dealing with…”).
Discipline: Same root thesis repeated across organs and symptoms—message consistency is a feature, not redundancy.
Proof language: personal reversal, “my community,” clinically validated framing, institution name-drops where used.
CTA style: Short imperative keywords; on Facebook, always points to Messenger + hidden/request folder instructions.
Examples observed (from public captions):
“Most people think kidney disease starts with the kidneys. It doesn’t. It often starts years earlier with metabolic damage.” (~56K views on TikTok grid capture)
Neuropathy story: symptoms → failed interventions → IR as upstream driver → nerves can repair when environment improves (~210.4K views; strong likes/comments/shares on detail open).
Fatty liver: “You can’t detox your way out of insulin resistance.” (~470.1K views)
FB CTAs: COMMENT “KIDNEY” / “READY” / “FIBER” / “YES” / “I’m ready” + DM follow-up.
4. Content Pillars
TikTok playlists make pillars explicit: Insulin Resistance (11) · Fiber & Nutrients (8) · Gut Health (5). The operational pillar map is broader:
Root-cause education — Insulin resistance biology; why symptoms cluster; cellular environment.
Condition bridges — Kidney, neuropathy, fatty liver, hypertension, lipids, anemia, cognitive risk, belly fat.
Myth vs mechanism — Incomplete BP stories (salt/stress only); cleanses vs true liver recovery; symptom management vs root cause (careful framing).
Protocol tools — Fiber, nutrients, fasting frameworks, “tools my community uses” (their commercial layer).
Proof & identity — Personal stories, community results, “fit people getting T2D” interrupts.
Conversion — Keyword comments, DMs, lives, link-in-bio.
Recommended PIW pillars
A — Insulin Resistance Explained (weekly teaching series)
B — Symptom → Root maps (energy, weight, labs, BP, liver enzymes, cravings)
C — What to do next (assessment, habits, accountability—PIW process)
D — Client/story & local trust (with consent)
E — Live Q&A / myth-bust sessions

TikTok Market Research
Capture date: August 4, 2026   |   Platform in scope: TikTok   |   Month 1 social listening
Executive Summary
The audience is not asking how to diet. They are asking why their effort stopped working, why they are tired, and who to believe.
Plateaus, fatigue and conflicting advice were the three most consistent frustrations heard across the research session.
"Progress beyond the scale" is an active, emotionally positive conversation the audience is already having, and it fits PIW's brand more cleanly than weight-loss language.
Insulin resistance, prediabetes, fatty liver and blood sugar are loud in this market. They are recorded here as market context only, not as PIW lead content.
Assessment-first language ("understand your body before another plan") matches how the audience already talks, which makes READY a natural next step.
Scope and Method

This report covers Month 1 of TikTok social listening, carried out in a single live session on August 4, 2026. Sixteen search terms were run across the metabolic health and sustainable weight-management space, and the Explore Fitness & Health and Education categories were reviewed.

Research was observation-only. No posts, likes, comments or follows were made. Where detailed engagement was not publicly visible, figures are marked accordingly or taken from search cards. No statistics were estimated or invented.
This document covers Month 1. Repeat the social-listening exercise every 30 days.

Editorial direction: Market insulin-resistance language is documented where it appears, but insulin-resistance-led content pillars are not recommended (Troy direction). Preferred PIW entry points remain metabolic health, plateaus, fatigue, personalized wellness and progress beyond the scale.
1. Audience Pain Points
Stalled progress despite real effort

The dominant frustration across plateau, mistakes and clinical searches. Creators repeatedly reframe this as an incomplete approach rather than a willpower failure, which suggests the audience arrives feeling personally blamed.
Examples: Doc Alvin plateau explainer  |  fat-loss-over-40 plateau reply
Always tired despite sleeping

Fatigue was its own dense search area, not a side note to weight. The audience looks for medical or lifestyle explanations — brain fog, survival mode, low energy — and treats tiredness as a problem worth solving in itself.
Examples: tired brain explainer  |  fatigue explainer
Confusion from conflicting advice

Myth-busting and "doctor explains" content draws consistent attention, indicating an audience that has heard too many contradictory rules and is looking for a trustworthy filter rather than more information.
Stubborn belly fat and the restart cycle
Recurring language around stubborn fat and starting over again after a plan fails. This is body-image sensitive territory and should be handled without shame.
2. Audience Desires
Simple, trustworthy education with a clear next step. Numbered lists and "do this" formats consistently drew attention across searches.
Proof of progress that is not the scale — energy, sleep, clothes fitting, strength and consistency.
Root-cause clarity before committing to another plan. "Watch this first" framing appeared repeatedly.
A personalized approach rather than a generic plan. The phrase "generic plans don't fit everyone" matches the frustration language directly.
Permission to stop blaming themselves. Compassionate reframing appeared repeatedly, while discipline-based messaging was less central to the observed conversation.
3. Common Questions
These are the questions the audience is typing. They were used as live search terms in this session and each returned an active content market.
Question the audience asks
What this signals
Why am I always tired?
Fatigue is a standalone entry point, equal in weight to weight-loss language.
Why can't I lose weight / why did I plateau?
High-intent frustration; the audience wants an explanation, not a plan.
Why do diets stop working?
Openness to a different approach; strong fit for assessment-first messaging.
What am I doing wrong?
Self-blame framing; requires a compassionate, non-shaming answer.
What does metabolic health actually mean?
Definition-level demand; room for plain-language authority.
How do I know if it is working if the scale has not moved?
Direct opening for non-scale progress content.
4. Language and Phrases Used
Using the audience's own wording improves both search discovery and the feeling of being understood.
Phrases the audience uses
"Stuck", "plateau", "nothing is working", "the scale won't move"
"Always tired", "no energy", "tired all the time even after sleeping"
"Doing it all wrong", "what I wish I knew", "mistakes"
"Non-scale victory", "more than the scale", "real progress"
"Personalized", "generic plans", "one-size-fits-all"
Hashtag language observed in this market
PIW-suited: #metabolichealth, #fatlossplateau, #MoreThanTheScale, #NonScaleVictory, #RealProgress, #healthtok, #LearnOnTikTok, #healthmyths.
Market clinical cluster observed (context only, not a recommended PIW stack): #insulinresistance, #PCOS, #prediabetes, #bloodsugar, #fattyliver.
General discovery tags such as #fyp and #foryou were present nearly everywhere and carry little strategic value on their own.
5. Misconceptions and Confusion
That stalled progress means personal failure, rather than an approach that no longer fits.
That the scale is the only valid measure of progress.
That a single food, drink or hack drives metabolic change. Listicle content in this space frequently over-promises.
That tiredness is normal and must simply be tolerated.
That a plan which worked for someone else should work for them.
Each of these is a myth-versus-fact opportunity that PIW can address with plain-language education and no medical claims.
